segments.text: We're gonna fly on this jet that costs half a million dollars per flight and we're also gonna fly on a $25,000 private jet, a $10,000 first-class seat, a blimp, and so much more.
segments.en: We're gonna fly on this jet that costs half a million dollars per flight and we're also gonna fly on a $25,000 private jet, a $10,000 first-class seat, a blimp, and so much more.
segments.zh: 我們要搭這架噴射機，一趟要價五十萬美元；同時也會坐兩萬五千美元的私人飛機、一萬美元的頭等艙、一艘飛船，還有更多驚喜。

tags.native: casual way to preview what's coming
tags.nativeZh: 口語預告接下來要做的事
examples: We're gonna try the new restaurant tonight.
We're gonna start with the easy part.
tags.usage: gonna = going to，預告行程時很常用。

tags.native: used to hint at extra surprises without listing them
tags.nativeZh: 暗示還有更多沒說完的內容
examples: The tour includes hotels, meals, and so much more.
The app has chat, maps, and so much more.
tags.usage: 預告或廣告結尾常用，把期待感留到後面。

segments.text: But before I show you what it's like to fly on some of the most luxurious planes on the planet, we're gonna fly on the cheapest plane in the world.
segments.en: But before I show you what it's like to fly on some of the most luxurious planes on the planet, we're gonna fly on the cheapest plane in the world.
segments.zh: 不過在帶你們看世界上最豪華的飛機是什麼感覺之前，我們先來坐全世界最便宜的飛機。

tags.native: used to delay the highlight and start with something else
tags.nativeZh: 先按下主菜、從別的地方開始
examples: But before I show you the results, let's look at the method.
But before we eat, let's wash up.
tags.usage: 影片或簡報常用：先賣關子，再切到對比項目。

tags.native: very comfortable, expensive, and fancy
examples: They stayed in a luxurious hotel.
It's comfortable, but not luxurious.
tags.usage: 比 fancy 更正式一點，強調舒適與昂貴。

segments.text: It's really rickety. Here's the dollar. I'm very nervous. Nothing to be nervous about. I've done this half a dozen times.
segments.en: It's really rickety. Here's the dollar. I'm very nervous. Nothing to be nervous about. I've done this half a dozen times.
segments.zh: 這東西真的很破爛。這就是那一塊錢。我超緊張。沒什麼好緊張的。這種我做過大概六次了。

tags.native: old, shaky, and not very sturdy
examples: We crossed a rickety old bridge.
Don't sit on that rickety chair.
tags.usage: 形容東西老舊不穩，帶點擔心它會散掉的感覺。

tags.native: a reassuring way to say it's safe or easy
tags.nativeZh: 安慰別人「沒什麼好緊張」
examples: It's just a short talk. Nothing to be nervous about.
You've practiced. Nothing to be nervous about.
tags.usage: 安慰語氣：把對方的擔心淡化。

tags.native: about six times; a casual count
examples: I've been there half a dozen times.
She called me half a dozen times today.
tags.usage: a dozen 是 12，half a dozen 就是 6，比直接說 six 更口語。

segments.text: You've done this six times?
segments.en: You've done this six times?
segments.zh: 你做過六次？

segments.text: Why does this sound like a lawn mower engine?
segments.en: Why does this sound like a lawn mower engine?
segments.zh: 為什麼這聽起來像割草機的引擎？

tags.native: a machine for cutting grass
examples: The lawn mower is in the garage.
That engine sounds like a lawn mower.
tags.usage: 這裡用來吐槽引擎聲又小又吵，不像正式飛機。

segments.text: Time for a ride on the world's cheapest plane ticket.
segments.en: Time for a ride on the world's cheapest plane ticket.
segments.zh: 來體驗全世界最便宜的機票吧。

segments.text: Oh boy. Oh my... Oh my gosh, round up. We're going so fast. — Come on, get it.
segments.en: Oh boy. Oh my... Oh my gosh, round up. We're going so fast. — Come on, get it.
segments.zh: 喔天哪。喔我的……我的天，加速。我們飛得好快。——加油，衝起來。

tags.native: a burst of surprise or alarm
tags.nativeZh: 驚訝或緊張時的口頭禪
examples: Oh my gosh, I forgot my passport.
Oh my gosh, look at that view.
tags.usage: 比 oh my god 稍微委婉，驚喜或驚嚇都能用。

tags.native: urging someone or something to succeed
examples: Come on, get it! You can lift that.
Come on, get it started.
tags.usage: 幫對方打氣，或催促機器／車輛快點啟動。

segments.text: That does not sound safe. — Nah ah. They almost hit the camera. Whoo! — What are you doing?
segments.en: That does not sound safe. — Nah ah. They almost hit the camera. Whoo! — What are you doing?
segments.zh: 這聽起來一點都不安全。——才不是。他們差點撞到攝影機。嗚呼！——你在幹嘛？

tags.native: a blunt way to say something feels dangerous
examples: That does not sound safe. Maybe we should stop.
Leaving the door open does not sound safe.
tags.usage: 用 does not 加強否定，語氣比 doesn't 更清楚、更認真。

tags.native: playful refusal; like 'nope' or 'nuh-uh'
tags.nativeZh: 俏皮地反駁「才不是／不行」
examples: Nah ah, that's my seat.
Nah ah, you're not leaving yet.
tags.usage: 口語、孩子氣一點的否認，寫成 nuh-uh / nah ah 都常見。

segments.text: Keep your seatbelt on. Uh, you just focused on keeping me alive, Doug. — I'm trying.
segments.en: Keep your seatbelt on. Uh, you just focused on keeping me alive, Doug. — I'm trying.
segments.zh: 安全帶繫好。呃，你就專心讓我活著就好，Doug。——我在努力了。

tags.native: a direct safety instruction
examples: Keep your seatbelt on until we stop.
The sign says to keep your seatbelt on.
tags.usage: keep … on 表示維持某個狀態，不要解開。

tags.native: jokingly depending on someone for safety
tags.nativeZh: 半開玩笑把性命託付給對方
examples: You just focus on keeping me alive in this game.
I'm counting on you to keep me alive.
tags.usage: 緊張場合常用的幽默：其實是在說「別讓我出事」。

segments.text: All right, he's in there. All right, dibs on the channel. I got what I need. You can land whenever. No.
segments.en: All right, he's in there. All right, dibs on the channel. I got what I need. You can land whenever. No.
segments.zh: 好，他上去了。好，這個頻道我先佔了。我要的畫面有了，你隨時可以降落。不行。

tags.native: a quick claim that something is yours first
examples: Dibs on the front seat!
I called dibs on the last cookie.
tags.usage: 口語：誰先喊 dibs，那東西就先歸誰。也可以說 call dibs on something。

tags.native: casual permission to do it at any time
tags.nativeZh: 隨你什麼時候做都可以
examples: I'm done here. You can leave whenever.
The file's saved. You can close it whenever.
tags.usage: whenever 單獨用，表示時間完全交給對方。

segments.text: Doug, come on. Doug, please. That guy pays my bills. Be careful.
segments.en: Doug, come on. Doug, please. That guy pays my bills. Be careful.
segments.zh: Doug，拜託啦。Doug，求你。那個人可是付我薪水的，小心一點。

tags.native: a joking reminder that someone is the boss / source of income
tags.nativeZh: 半開玩笑說對方是衣食父母
examples: Be nice. That client pays my bills.
I can't roast the host. He pays my bills.
tags.usage: 用來提醒：這人很重要，別鬧出事。

segments.text: And if you guys think this is crazy, wait until later in the video when we have the world's most expensive plane ticket on the planet. Wait a minute, you're making me feel bad. Oh my god, he's coming in hot. [Doug] Get ready to land.
segments.en: And if you guys think this is crazy, wait until later in the video when we have the world's most expensive plane ticket on the planet. Wait a minute, you're making me feel bad. Oh my god, he's coming in hot. [Doug] Get ready to land.
segments.zh: 如果你們覺得這已經很瘋了，等到影片後面，我們還有全世界最貴的機票。等一下，你這樣講我會不好意思。天啊，他要高速進場了。[Doug] 準備降落。

tags.v: wait until later in the video
tags.native: a teaser that something bigger is coming
tags.nativeZh: 預告後面還有更精彩的
examples: This is wild, but wait until later in the video.
Wait until later in the video for the reveal.
tags.usage: YouTube 常用留人句：先給一點，再把高潮往後放。

tags.native: arriving fast, hard, or aggressively
tags.nativeZh: 高速／猛烈地靠近或進場
examples: The plane is coming in hot.
He came in hot and almost missed the turn.
tags.usage: 航空、賽車、遊戲都常用，帶一點「有點太快、有點危險」的感覺。

segments.text: Almost. [Group] Yeah. We're on the ground, we survive. [Person] Our next plane is the $1,000 first class plane ticket.
segments.en: Almost. [Group] Yeah. We're on the ground, we survive. [Person] Our next plane is the $1,000 first class plane ticket.
segments.zh: 快了。[眾人] 耶。我們著地了，活下來了。[旁白] 下一架是一千美元的頭等艙機票。

tags.v: We're on the ground, we survive.
tags.native: a relieved, slightly joking way to say they made it
tags.nativeZh: 鬆一口氣：我們活著著陸了
examples: We're on the ground. We made it.
The ride's over. We survived.
tags.usage: 官方字幕是 we survive，口語裡更常說 we survived / we made it。

segments.text: But here's the thing, boys. I bought all the first class seats, so, sit wherever you want. Would you like some miracle mist lotion? Why?
segments.en: But here's the thing, boys. I bought all the first class seats, so, sit wherever you want. Would you like some miracle mist lotion? Why?
segments.zh: 不過重點來了，兄弟們。頭等艙座位我全買下來了，所以你們愛坐哪就坐哪。要來點奇蹟噴霧乳液嗎？為什麼？

tags.native: used to introduce the key point or catch
examples: Here's the thing: we only have ten minutes.
I'd love to go, but here's the thing — I have a test.
tags.usage: 先把聽眾注意力拉回來，再講真正重要的那句。

tags.native: complete freedom to choose a seat
examples: The room is ours. Sit wherever you want.
There are no assigned seats, so sit wherever you want.
tags.usage: wherever 強調沒有限制，很適合輕鬆招待別人。

segments.text: Because first class, baby, fine dining, huh. [Person] Each of us has our own seat and TV. The ticket also comes with a decent meal, a free bag of toiletries and pajamas.
segments.en: Because first class, baby, fine dining, huh. [Person] Each of us has our own seat and TV. The ticket also comes with a decent meal, a free bag of toiletries and pajamas.
segments.zh: 因為這是頭等艙啊寶貝，精品餐飲，對吧。[旁白] 我們每個人都有自己的座位和電視。機票還附一頓還不錯的餐、一包免費盥洗用品和睡衣。

tags.native: small bathroom items like toothpaste or lotion
examples: Don't forget your toiletries.
The hotel provides basic toiletries.
tags.usage: 複數名詞，泛指旅行用的洗漱小物。

tags.native: clothes worn for sleeping
examples: I packed my pajamas.
Some first-class tickets come with pajamas.
tags.usage: 美式拼法 pajamas；英式常寫 pyjamas。

segments.text: Do we get to take all this home with us? [Person] And during longer flights... Recline. We should recline into a bed.
segments.en: Do we get to take all this home with us? [Person] And during longer flights... Recline. We should recline into a bed.
segments.zh: 這些我們都可以帶回家嗎？[旁白] 而且在較長的航班上……放倒。我們應該把座位放倒變成床。

tags.native: to lean a seat back into a flatter position
examples: You can recline your seat after takeoff.
Don't recline too far if someone is behind you.
tags.usage: 搭機、看電影時常用：recline the seat / recline into a bed。

segments.text: I feel like I'm in a coffin, which I like. Yeah, this is crazy. [Person] And best of all... My favorite part about this $1,000 plane, I don't need to speak to Nolan.
segments.en: I feel like I'm in a coffin, which I like. Yeah, this is crazy. [Person] And best of all... My favorite part about this $1,000 plane, I don't need to speak to Nolan.
segments.zh: 我覺得自己好像躺在棺材裡，不過我喜歡。對，這太狂了。[旁白] 最棒的是……這一千美元班機我最喜歡的部分是：我不必跟 Nolan 講話。

tags.v: I feel like I'm in a coffin
tags.native: a jokey complaint that a space is tight and enclosed
tags.nativeZh: 開玩笑抱怨空間又窄又密
examples: In the bottom bunk I feel like I'm in a coffin.
This changing room is so tiny I feel like I'm in a coffin.
tags.usage: 誇張比喻，聽起來負面，但這裡立刻補 which I like，變成幽默。

tags.native: used to introduce the most attractive point
examples: It's cheap, and best of all, it's nearby.
Best of all, we don't have to wait.
tags.usage: 列完優點後再加一記高潮，口語和廣告都很常見。

segments.text: I don't like this glass 'cause it like separates me. I'm all alone back here. That is the exact reason why I like it.
segments.en: I don't like this glass 'cause it like separates me. I'm all alone back here. That is the exact reason why I like it.
segments.zh: 我不喜歡這塊玻璃，因為它好像把我隔開了。我一個人待在後面。這正是我喜歡它的原因。

tags.native: spoken short form of because
examples: I'm leaving early 'cause I'm tired.
I like it 'cause it's quiet.
tags.usage: 只能用在口語或很輕鬆的文字，寫正式句子仍用 because。

tags.v: That is the exact reason why…
tags.native: emphatically pointing to the precise cause
examples: That's the exact reason why I left early.
This is the exact reason why we practiced.
tags.usage: 比 that's why 更用力，帶點「你講的點正好是關鍵」。

segments.text: The only downside is that you don't get a lot of privacy. [Chris] It's really awkward filming a video with all these people walking by. So, let's see what a plane ticket 10 times more expensive will feel like.
segments.en: The only downside is that you don't get a lot of privacy. [Chris] It's really awkward filming a video with all these people walking by. So, let's see what a plane ticket 10 times more expensive will feel like.
segments.zh: 唯一的缺點是隱私不多。[Chris] 這麼多人走過，要拍影片真的很尷尬。那我們來看看貴十倍的機票會是什麼感覺。

tags.native: the disadvantage or catch
examples: The downside is the price.
Every plan has a downside.
tags.usage: 常用 The only downside is… 先肯定再補一句缺點。

tags.native: uncomfortable or embarrassing
examples: It got awkward when nobody spoke.
Filming in public can feel awkward.
tags.usage: 社交場合很常用，不一定是壞事，但氣氛別扭。

segments.text: And now, the $10,000 plane ticket. Oh man, this is nice. I have unlimited legroom here.
segments.en: And now, the $10,000 plane ticket. Oh man, this is nice. I have unlimited legroom here.
segments.zh: 接下來，一萬美元的機票。喔天，這很舒服。這裡有無限的伸腿空間。

tags.native: space for your legs in a seat
examples: I booked an exit row for more legroom.
The back seats have almost no legroom.
tags.usage: 談飛機、汽車座位舒適度的核心詞；unlimited legroom 是誇張讚美。

segments.text: Look, let's start off by analyzing what we get. A tablet, a giant touchscreen TV, my own in-seat drink bar, snacks.
segments.en: Look, let's start off by analyzing what we get. A tablet, a giant touchscreen TV, my own in-seat drink bar, snacks.
segments.zh: 來，我們先盤點一下有什麼。一台平板、超大觸控電視、專屬座位飲料吧，還有零食。

tags.native: a casual way to begin a series of steps
examples: Let's start off by checking the list.
Let's start off by introducing ourselves.
tags.usage: start off 等於「開頭先做這件事」，簡報、教學、開箱都很順。

tags.native: built into or located at your seat
tags.nativeZh: 附在座位上的、座位內建的
examples: The in-seat screen is bigger than I expected.
Some trains have in-seat power outlets.
tags.usage: 複合形容詞，強調不用起身、就在座位旁。

segments.text: This isn't Feastables chocolate. I want a refund. We're getting connected to the Wi-Fi. We might have paid $10,000 for our seat but we still have to pay $20 for Wi-Fi.
segments.en: This isn't Feastables chocolate. I want a refund. We're getting connected to the Wi-Fi. We might have paid $10,000 for our seat but we still have to pay $20 for Wi-Fi.
segments.zh: 這不是 Feastables 巧克力。我要退款。我們正在連 Wi-Fi。座位花了一萬美元，Wi-Fi 居然還要再付二十美元。

tags.native: a joking or real demand to get money back
tags.nativeZh: 要求退款（這裡是開玩笑）
examples: This isn't what I ordered. I want a refund.
If the Wi-Fi keeps dropping, I want a refund.
tags.usage: 正式場合也能用；這裡是看到不是自家巧克力後的笑點。

segments.text: It's not free? Now, we're taking off, which is pretty crazy because I can literally watch it on my TV. Look at how nice this bathroom is.
segments.en: It's not free? Now, we're taking off, which is pretty crazy because I can literally watch it on my TV. Look at how nice this bathroom is.
segments.zh: 不是免費的嗎？現在起飛了，這挺瘋狂的，因為我可以直接在自己的電視上看起飛畫面。你看這洗手間有多講究。

tags.native: emphasizing that something is actually, not just figuratively, true
tags.nativeZh: 強調「真的可以、不是誇張」
examples: I can literally see the runway from here.
We can literally finish this in five minutes.
tags.usage: 口語裡 literally 常拿來加強語氣，這裡則是字面意思：真的能在螢幕上來看。

segments.text: You have a sink, a toilet, and then a shower. That is crazy. Look at that.
segments.en: You have a sink, a toilet, and then a shower. That is crazy. Look at that.
segments.zh: 有洗手台、馬桶，還有淋浴間。這太狂了。你看那個。

segments.text: We are 30,000 feet in the air and I can take a shower. On top of that, me and the boys can order as much gourmet food as we want.
segments.en: We are 30,000 feet in the air and I can take a shower. On top of that, me and the boys can order as much gourmet food as we want.
segments.zh: 我們在三萬英尺高空，我還能洗澡。除此之外，我和兄弟們還能隨便點高級餐點。

tags.native: used to add another impressive or extra point
examples: The room is huge. On top of that, it has a view.
He was late, and on top of that, he forgot the keys.
tags.usage: 可加好消息也可加壞消息，重點是「再叠加一層」。

tags.native: high-end or especially high-quality food
examples: They served gourmet meals on the flight.
It's a small but gourmet restaurant.
tags.usage: 多半放在 food / meal / chocolate 前面，語氣比 delicious 更「高級」。

segments.text: And that's not all, we save the best for last. Hey, how's it going? There's a private lounge in the back of the plane. Hey, Jimmy.
segments.en: And that's not all, we save the best for last. Hey, how's it going? There's a private lounge in the back of the plane. Hey, Jimmy.
segments.zh: 這還沒完，壓軸的留到最後。嘿，你好嗎？機尾還有一間私人休息室。嘿，Jimmy。

tags.native: a teaser that something even better is coming
examples: That's not all — there's dessert too.
The prize is a ticket, and that's not all.
tags.usage: 常跟 we saved the best for last 連用，製造期待。

tags.native: to keep the most impressive thing until the end
examples: Let's save the best for last.
They saved the best surprise for last.
tags.usage: 展示、送禮、說故事都很常用的節奏句。

segments.text: Yeah. Ow. You're not dreaming. That was the $10,000 plane ticket.
segments.en: Yeah. Ow. You're not dreaming. That was the $10,000 plane ticket.
segments.zh: 嗯。啊。你不是在做夢。那就是一萬美元的機票。

tags.native: used to confirm something unbelievable is real
tags.nativeZh: 提醒「這是真的，不是做夢」
examples: You're not dreaming. That's actually the ocean.
Pinch yourself. You're not dreaming.
tags.usage: 看到超乎尋常的東西時，用來加強真實感。

segments.text: Point the camera up and down. And now we're at the $25,000 plane ticket that is up these stairs.
segments.en: Point the camera up and down. And now we're at the $25,000 plane ticket that is up these stairs.
segments.zh: 鏡頭上下掃一下。現在我們來到兩萬五千美元的機票，要從這段樓梯上去。

segments.text: That's right, there's floors. This is insane. This is crazy. We're gonna be sitting above other people. Oh my god.
segments.en: That's right, there's floors. This is insane. This is crazy. We're gonna be sitting above other people. Oh my god.
segments.zh: 沒錯，這飛機是有樓層的。這太誇張了。這太狂了。我們會坐在其他人頭上。我的天。

tags.native: confirming a surprising fact
tags.nativeZh: 證實一個讓人意外的事實
examples: That's right, we get tomorrow off.
That's right — there's a second floor.
tags.usage: 先丟出驚人資訊，再用 that's right 幫聽眾確認自己沒聽錯。

segments.text: Now, this is your room. For $25,000, you get two massive rooms. Oh, this is crazy. I've never seen anything like this.
segments.en: Now, this is your room. For $25,000, you get two massive rooms. Oh, this is crazy. I've never seen anything like this.
segments.zh: 現在，這是你的房間。花兩萬五千美元，你會得到兩個超大房間。喔，這太狂了。我從來沒見過這種東西。

tags.v: I've never seen anything like this.
tags.native: strong surprise at something new or extreme
tags.nativeZh: 表示見過最誇張／從未見過
examples: I've never seen anything like this in a hotel.
Wow, I've never seen anything like this.
tags.usage: 讚嘆句，比重複說 crazy / insane 更完整。

segments.text: Holy... Our space on this plane is literally four times bigger than the last one. I've never seen a plane where I can comfortably do jumping jacks.
segments.en: Holy... Our space on this plane is literally four times bigger than the last one. I've never seen a plane where I can comfortably do jumping jacks.
segments.zh: 我的天……我們在這架飛機上的空間，簡直比上一架大四倍。我從沒見過一架飛機能讓我舒舒服服地做開合跳。

tags.native: emphasizing a real, measurable jump in size
examples: This apartment is literally twice as big.
The new screen is literally four times bigger.
tags.usage: times bigger 用來做倍數比較；前面加 literally 是在說「不是誇張」。

tags.native: an exercise of jumping with arms and legs spread
examples: We started with twenty jumping jacks.
There isn't room to do jumping jacks.
tags.usage: 用來形容空間大到可以在飛機上做操。

segments.text: Look at this. We also get two chairs, a ton of TVs. There are more TVs in this one room than all of the other planes we've been on.
segments.en: Look at this. We also get two chairs, a ton of TVs. There are more TVs in this one room than all of the other planes we've been on.
segments.zh: 你看這個。我們還有兩張椅子、超多台電視。這一個房間的電視，比我們坐過的其他飛機加起來還多。

tags.native: a casual way to say a lot of
examples: There's a ton of snacks in the kitchen.
I have a ton of emails to answer.
tags.usage: 比 a lot of 更誇張一點，不適合正式報告。

segments.text: Food served by a personal flight attendant. Why is it that after a certain price point, they always give you a caviar?
segments.en: Food served by a personal flight attendant. Why is it that after a certain price point, they always give you a caviar?
segments.zh: 餐點由專屬空服員送上。為什麼到了某個價位之後，他們總是會給你魚子醬？

tags.native: a crew member who serves passengers on a plane
examples: The flight attendant brought more water.
She works as a flight attendant.
tags.usage: 比空姊／空少更中性、通用的說法。

tags.native: a particular level of cost
examples: At this price point, I'd expect better quality.
They're aiming at a lower price point.
tags.usage: 討論商品值不值得時常用：after a certain price point…

tags.native: expensive fish roe served as a luxury food
examples: They served caviar at the reception.
Caviar is a classic luxury snack.
tags.usage: 常被當成「有錢人才吃」的象徵，影片裡用來吐槽豪華套餐。

segments.text: And the bathroom. — Can we talk about something? This bathroom is like a disappointment.
segments.en: And the bathroom. — Can we talk about something? This bathroom is like a disappointment.
segments.zh: 還有洗手間。——我們能說件事嗎？這洗手間有點讓人失望。

tags.native: a way to switch topics or finally raise a complaint
tags.nativeZh: 想換話題或終於要吐槽時用
examples: Can we talk about something? This chair is broken.
Can we talk about the plan for tomorrow?
tags.usage: 表面是徵求討論，實際常常是要講一個不快的重點。

tags.native: something that is worse than expected
examples: The ending was a disappointment.
The bathroom was a bit of a disappointment.
tags.usage: 可指心情，也可直接指那個讓人失望的東西。

segments.text: No shower, no heated floors, half the size. I think the $10,000 flight was a better price point.
segments.en: No shower, no heated floors, half the size. I think the $10,000 flight was a better price point.
segments.zh: 沒有淋浴、沒有加熱地板，才一半大。我覺得一萬美元那班的性價比比較好。

tags.native: floors with built-in warming
examples: The bathroom has heated floors.
Heated floors feel amazing in winter.
tags.usage: 豪華住宅或溫泉旅館常見配備，這裡拿來當比較基準。

tags.native: better value for the money
tags.nativeZh: 更划算的價位／性價比更好
examples: The mid-range model is a better price point.
For me, the smaller room is a better price point.
tags.usage: 不一定是更便宜，而是「這個價錢更值得」。

segments.text: Would you pay this kind of money for a single flight? I wouldn't recommend this. I would recommend a car. Buy a car instead.
segments.en: Would you pay this kind of money for a single flight? I wouldn't recommend this. I would recommend a car. Buy a car instead.
segments.zh: 你會為單程飛機花這種錢嗎？我不會建議這樣。我會建議買車。改買車吧。

tags.native: a polite but clear way to advise against something
examples: I wouldn't recommend this restaurant at night.
For a short trip, I wouldn't recommend the upgrade.
tags.usage: 比 Don't do it 更客氣，適合給建議。

segments.text: And now, the best part of the room, a queen size bed. Ooh.
segments.en: And now, the best part of the room, a queen size bed. Ooh.
segments.zh: 接著是房間最棒的部分：一張加大雙人床。喔。

tags.native: a large bed, bigger than a double but smaller than a king
examples: The room has a queen size bed.
We upgraded to a queen size bed.
tags.usage: 飯店和機票比較常寫 queen-size bed，口語連在一起說即可。

segments.text: Why don't they just make every seat a bed? Bro, instead of three seats side by side, just put a bunk bed with three beds.
segments.en: Why don't they just make every seat a bed? Bro, instead of three seats side by side, just put a bunk bed with three beds.
segments.zh: 為什麼他們不直接讓每個座位都是床？兄弟，與其三個座位並排，直接放個三層床就好了。

tags.native: casual address among friends, often before a joke or idea
examples: Bro, that's a terrible idea.
Bro, just take the day off.
tags.usage: 年輕人口語，不一定真的是兄弟，用來拉近距離。

tags.native: two or more beds stacked vertically
examples: The kids share a bunk bed.
A bunk bed would save a lot of space.
tags.usage: 一般是兩層；這裡說 three beds，是在開玩笑要做三層。

segments.text: Good morning. That was really good sleep. Karl, wake up. We're gonna land. I slept like a rock.
segments.en: Good morning. That was really good sleep. Karl, wake up. We're gonna land. I slept like a rock.
segments.zh: 早安。剛剛睡得真好。Karl，起床了，我們要降落了。我睡得像石頭一樣沉。

tags.native: slept very deeply and well
examples: After the hike, I slept like a rock.
I usually toss and turn, but last night I slept like a rock.
tags.usage: 和 slept like a baby 類似，強調一躺就睡、不容易醒。

segments.text: That was the world's most expensive commercial flight. Time for private flights.
segments.en: That was the world's most expensive commercial flight. Time for private flights.
segments.zh: 那就是全世界最貴的商業航班。接下來輪到私人包機。

tags.native: a regular airline flight, not a private one
examples: It was my first commercial flight in years.
Private jets are faster than commercial flights.
tags.usage: 和 private flight / private jet 對比時特別常用。

segments.text: This is the $100,000 plane. This thing's huge. At this price point, you get the entire plane.
segments.en: This is the $100,000 plane. This thing's huge. At this price point, you get the entire plane.
segments.zh: 這是十萬美元的飛機。這傢伙好大。到了這個價位，整架飛機都是你的。

tags.native: informal amazement at size
examples: This thing's huge. Will it fit in the car?
Look at that burger. This thing's huge.
tags.usage: thing 可隨便指眼前的大物件，不必先講正式名稱。

tags.native: the whole aircraft is yours
examples: For this price, you get the entire cabin.
On a charter, you get the entire plane.
tags.usage: 用來對比前面只能買一個座位的商業航班。

segments.text: Private, private. Oh, it's like a yacht. This is wild. This is unbelievable.
segments.en: Private, private. Oh, it's like a yacht. This is wild. This is unbelievable.
segments.zh: 私人的、私人的。喔，好像遊艇。這太狂了。這簡直難以置信。

tags.native: this is amazing, crazy, or hard to believe
tags.nativeZh: 這太狂了、太不可思議了
examples: The view from up here is wild.
This is wild. I can't believe we got in.
tags.usage: 年輕人口語，情緒可以是讚嘆或難以置信。

tags.native: so extreme it is hard to accept as real
examples: The scale of this jet is unbelievable.
She did an unbelievable job.
tags.usage: 正面負面都能用，這裡是純粹驚嘆。

segments.text: You wanna know the craziest part? This is just one of four rooms. [Karl] There's more to the plane, I thought this was it. Guys, come over here.
segments.en: You wanna know the craziest part? This is just one of four rooms. [Karl] There's more to the plane, I thought this was it. Guys, come over here.
segments.zh: 你想知道最瘋狂的部分嗎？這只是四個房間裡的其中一間。[Karl] 飛機還有更多地方，我還以為就這樣了。各位，過來這邊。

tags.v: You wanna know the craziest part?
tags.native: a hook before an even more surprising detail
tags.nativeZh: 先問一句再丟出更狂的資訊
examples: You wanna know the craziest part? It's free.
Wanna know the craziest part? He already left.
tags.usage: wanna = want to，說故事時很好用的轉折。

segments.text: What room is this? This is literally another lounge area with a bunch of snacks and a huge TV. And if you're feeling tired, you get your own private bedroom.
segments.en: What room is this? This is literally another lounge area with a bunch of snacks and a huge TV. And if you're feeling tired, you get your own private bedroom.
segments.zh: 這是什麼房間？這簡直是另一個休息區，有一堆零食和超大電視。如果你覺得累了，還有自己的私人臥室。

tags.native: a comfortable space for sitting and relaxing
examples: The hotel lounge area is quieter at night.
There's a lounge area with snacks and a TV.
tags.usage: 機場、飯店、私人飛機都常用 lounge 指休息空間。

segments.text: Dude, what? Wee. This is like a hotel. And last but not least, the bathroom.
segments.en: Dude, what? Wee. This is like a hotel. And last but not least, the bathroom.
segments.zh: 老兄，什麼？吁。這好像飯店。最後但同樣重要的是：洗手間。

tags.native: used before the final item so it still feels important
examples: Last but not least, thank you to the crew.
And last but not least, the dessert.
tags.usage: 列舉結尾超常用，避免最後一項聽起來像隨便帶過。

segments.text: Three, shut your mouth right now. Shut it. Whoa. — This is insane. There's a seat in the bathroom. Dibs. Have you ever even seen a jet half this size?
segments.en: Three, shut your mouth right now. Shut it. Whoa. — This is insane. There's a seat in the bathroom. Dibs. Have you ever even seen a jet half this size?
segments.zh: 三，現在立刻閉嘴。閉上。哇。——這太誇張了。洗手間裡還有座位。我先佔了。你有見過一半這麼大的噴射機嗎？

tags.native: a very blunt command to stop talking, often playful among friends
tags.nativeZh: 叫人立刻閉嘴（朋友間常是開玩笑）
examples: Shut your mouth right now, you're going to spoil it.
I told him to shut his mouth before he laughed.
tags.usage: 語氣很重，不適合對陌生人或正式場合；這裡是看到超豪華廁所時的興奮吐槽。

tags.native: claiming something first
examples: Dibs on the window seat.
There's a seat in there. Dibs.
tags.usage: 可以單獨喊一聲 Dibs，不必每次都說 dibs on something。

segments.text: No. — Never. What do we talk about while on our private jet? Well, I'll tell you, last year I had sold the (indistinct).
segments.en: No. — Never. What do we talk about while on our private jet? Well, I'll tell you, last year I had sold the (indistinct).
segments.zh: 沒有。——從來沒有。在私人飛機上我們該聊什麼？跟你說，去年我賣掉了那個（聽不清）。

segments.text: Oh no. Oh, wait. I just realized I'm taking off backwards. Whoa. — GoPro.
segments.en: Oh no. Oh, wait. I just realized I'm taking off backwards. Whoa. — GoPro.
segments.zh: 喔不。喔，等一下。我才發現我是倒著起飛的。哇。——GoPro。

tags.native: used when a fact suddenly becomes clear
examples: I just realized I left my phone in the car.
Wait. I just realized we're early.
tags.usage: 常跟 oh wait / oh no 連用，適合描述當下的頓悟。

segments.text: I didn't realize we were taking off. Not the camera. Stop! This might be the best bathroom yet. This is the toilet.
segments.en: I didn't realize we were taking off. Not the camera. Stop! This might be the best bathroom yet. This is the toilet.
segments.zh: 我沒意識到我們起飛了。攝影機別動。停！這可能是目前最棒的洗手間。這是馬桶。

tags.native: admitting you only just noticed what was happening
examples: I didn't realize we were already late.
I didn't realize we were on camera.
tags.usage: 比 I didn't know 更著重「過程中沒注意」。

segments.text: On the toilet you can watch TV. Hey, Nolan, I hope you feel comfortable in the bathroom. What's going on? I'm so confused.
segments.en: On the toilet you can watch TV. Hey, Nolan, I hope you feel comfortable in the bathroom. What's going on? I'm so confused.
segments.zh: 坐在馬桶上還能看電視。嘿，Nolan，希望你在洗手間裡覺得舒適。發生什麼事？我好困惑。

tags.native: a polite or teasing wish that someone is at ease
tags.nativeZh: 希望你覺得自在（也可帶調侃）
examples: I hope you feel comfortable in the new office.
I hope you feel comfortable speaking up.
tags.usage: 字面是關心，這裡是朋友把人關在廁所時的好笑禮貌話。

segments.text: No, no. He's never getting out. What? — Oh wow.
segments.en: No, no. He's never getting out. What? — Oh wow.
segments.zh: 不行，不行。他永遠出不來了。什麼？——喔哇。

tags.native: a joking exaggeration that someone is stuck
tags.nativeZh: 誇張地說對方出不來了
examples: If he sits on that sofa, he's never getting out.
Once she starts that game, she's never getting out.
tags.usage: 用現在進行式 getting，聽起來像眼前正在發生、而且沒完沒了。

segments.text: I have steak, mashed potatoes, and veggies. And you guys inspired me a little bit, so I brought some pizza.
segments.en: I have steak, mashed potatoes, and veggies. And you guys inspired me a little bit, so I brought some pizza.
segments.zh: 我有牛排、薯泥和蔬菜。你們也啟發我了一點，所以我帶了披薩。

tags.native: crediting friends for giving you an idea
tags.nativeZh: 說是因為你們我才有這個想法
examples: You guys inspired me to cook tonight.
Your trip inspired me to start packing.
tags.usage: 輕鬆感謝或開玩笑的說法，不一定是很嚴肅的啟發。

segments.text: [Group] Yeah!
segments.en: [Group] Yeah!
segments.zh: [眾人] 耶！

segments.text: This is my favorite plane because it has YouTube but we didn't pop up first, so now, it's not. You can tell this is a rich person bed 'cause there's like 500 pillows. This one outta here. That one outta here.
segments.en: This is my favorite plane because it has YouTube but we didn't pop up first, so now, it's not. You can tell this is a rich person bed 'cause there's like 500 pillows. This one outta here. That one outta here.
segments.zh: 這是我最喜歡的飛機，因為它有 YouTube，但我們沒有排在第一個，所以現在我不喜歡了。你看得出來這是有錢人的床，因為大概有五百顆枕頭。這一顆拿走。那一顆也拿走。

tags.native: we didn't appear at the top of the list or search results
tags.nativeZh: 沒有排在最前面／沒有第一個出現
examples: Our video didn't pop up first in the search.
If the app doesn't pop up first, people miss it.
tags.usage: pop up 是突然出現；這裡指 YouTube 推薦或搜尋排序。

tags.native: casual 'out of here'; get this out / I'm leaving
tags.nativeZh: 口語的 out of here：拿走或離開
examples: This pillow is outta here.
I'm outta here after lunch.
tags.usage: 把 out of 連成 outta，很口語。這裡是把多餘枕頭丟掉。

segments.text: I'm gonna fly this thingy. And that's the beauty of flying private. You can do whatever you want whenever.
segments.en: I'm gonna fly this thingy. And that's the beauty of flying private. You can do whatever you want whenever.
segments.zh: 我來開這東西。這就是坐私人飛機的美妙之處：你想做什麼、什麼時候做都可以。

tags.native: that's the especially good thing about it
examples: That's the beauty of working from home.
That's the beauty of flying private: you set the schedule.
tags.usage: 先講規則或限制，再用這句點出最大優點。

tags.native: at any time you like
examples: You can call me whenever.
Do whatever you want, whenever you want.
tags.usage: 和 whatever 連用時，強調完全自由、沒有時間限制。

segments.text: Karl's flying the plane, Chandler's jamming out the pizza. Chris is taking a nap and I don't even know where Nolan went.
segments.en: Karl's flying the plane, Chandler's jamming out the pizza. Chris is taking a nap and I don't even know where Nolan went.
segments.zh: Karl 在開飛機，Chandler 一邊吃披薩一邊嗨，Chris 在小睡，我甚至不知道 Nolan 去哪了。

tags.native: happily playing or enjoying music, often loudly
tags.nativeZh: 盡情沉浸在音樂裡、跟著嗨
examples: He was jamming out in the car.
They're jamming out to that new album.
tags.usage: 不一定真的在演奏，聽音樂很投入也可以說 jam out。

segments.text: There's no layovers when you fly private and there's no TSA, so you save tons of time. Hence why? Basically, every rich person you know owns a private jet. Hey, guys. — Yeah.
segments.en: There's no layovers when you fly private and there's no TSA, so you save tons of time. Hence why? Basically, every rich person you know owns a private jet. Hey, guys. — Yeah.
segments.zh: 坐私人飛機沒有轉機，也沒有 TSA 安檢，所以能省下超多時間。正因如此？基本上你認識的每個有錢人都有私人飛機。嘿，各位。——嗯。

tags.native: stops between flights on the way to a destination
examples: The ticket is cheap, but there are two layovers.
I hate long layovers at night.
tags.usage: 私人飛機常被拿來對比「不用轉機」。單數是 layover。

tags.native: U.S. airport security agency; often used for the security check itself
tags.nativeZh: 美國運輸安全管理局，也泛指機場安檢
examples: We got through TSA faster than usual.
There's no TSA when you fly private.
tags.usage: 口語常直接說 go through TSA，不一定要把全名念出來。

tags.native: a slightly clumsy spoken stand-in for 'that's why'
tags.nativeZh: 口誤／口語版的「所以才會這樣」
examples: That's why every rich person owns a jet.
Hence the long lines at security.
tags.usage: 標準用法是 Hence 或 That's why。影片裡的 Hence why? 是隨口轉折，學的時候建議改用 That's why。

segments.text: We're gonna land soon. Wait, wait. Is Nolan still in the bathroom? I don't know, really. Karl, go let him out.
segments.en: We're gonna land soon. Wait, wait. Is Nolan still in the bathroom? I don't know, really. Karl, go let him out.
segments.zh: 我們快要降落了。等一下、等一下。Nolan 還在洗手間嗎？我真的不知道。Karl，去放他出來。

tags.native: tell someone to go and release another person
examples: Go let him out of the room.
Can you go let the dog out?
tags.usage: go + 原形動詞，口語裡用來支使旁邊的人立刻去做。

segments.text: Oh, oh. — How was your flight? Still better than the $1000 plane. And now, the $300,000 blimp.
segments.en: Oh, oh. — How was your flight? Still better than the $1000 plane. And now, the $300,000 blimp.
segments.zh: 喔、喔。——班機感覺如何？還是比那一千美元的飛機好。接下來，三十萬美元的飛船。

tags.native: the standard greeting after someone lands
examples: How was your flight? Any delays?
How was your flight? You look exhausted.
tags.usage: 這裡是把人從廁所放出來後的玩笑問候。

segments.text: I'll unblur it in a second. Before I remove your blindfolds, what do you think is on the side of the blimp? Is it Nolan's phone number?
segments.en: I'll unblur it in a second. Before I remove your blindfolds, what do you think is on the side of the blimp? Is it Nolan's phone number?
segments.zh: 我等一下會取消模糊。在我拿掉眼罩之前，你們覺得飛船側面是什麼？是 Nolan 的電話號碼嗎？

tags.native: to remove a blur effect so something becomes visible
tags.nativeZh: 取消模糊、讓畫面變清楚
examples: I'll unblur the image in a second.
The app can unblur text on the sign.
tags.usage: 網路影片常用：先模糊避免劇透，再說 unblur it。

tags.native: covers placed over the eyes so someone cannot see
examples: They put on blindfolds before the surprise.
Don't take the blindfold off yet.
tags.usage: 驚喜環節的經典道具；take off / remove your blindfolds。

segments.text: Did you do Nolan's phone number? That would be funny. — Next time. Take off your blindfolds. Turn around.
segments.en: Did you do Nolan's phone number? That would be funny. — Next time. Take off your blindfolds. Turn around.
segments.zh: 你真的弄了 Nolan 的電話號碼？那會很好笑。——下次。拿下眼罩。轉過身。

tags.native: reacting to a hypothetical joke or prank
tags.nativeZh: 覺得那個假設會很好笑
examples: If they printed his number on the side, that would be funny.
That would be funny, but maybe next time.
tags.usage: would 表示還沒發生、只是想像。

tags.native: a short way to postpone an idea or promise it later
examples: Not today. Next time.
I'll try the spicy one next time.
tags.usage: 可以是承諾，也可以是俏皮地拒絕。

segments.text: I heart Karl's mom. Hold up. Why? He really loves my mom.
segments.en: I heart Karl's mom. Hold up. Why? He really loves my mom.
segments.zh: 我給 Karl 的媽媽一顆愛心。等一下。為什麼？他是真的愛我媽。

tags.native: internet-style 'I love …', like a heart emoji
tags.nativeZh: 網路口語：用愛心表示喜歡
examples: I heart this song.
She wrote 'I heart New York' on the cup.
tags.usage: heart 當動詞，來自 I ❤，比 I love 更輕、更玩笑。

tags.native: wait a second; pause to question something
examples: Hold up, did he just say that?
Hold up. Why is my name on the board?
tags.usage: 發現不對勁或很好笑時，先喊停再追問。

segments.text: No, Karl, he hearts your mom. He doesn't love your mom. That'd be weird. — No, I love her. Oh. Dude, am I pushing it right now?
segments.en: No, Karl, he hearts your mom. He doesn't love your mom. That'd be weird. — No, I love her. Oh. Dude, am I pushing it right now?
segments.zh: 不，Karl，他是「愛心」你媽，不是愛你媽。那樣會很怪。——不，我就是愛她。喔。老兄，我是不是有點過頭了？

tags.native: a quick reaction that something would feel socially off
examples: If I texted her boss, that'd be weird.
Showing up unannounced would be weird.
tags.usage: That'd = that would，用來迅速表達界線。

tags.v: am I pushing it right now?
tags.native: asking if you're going a bit too far
tags.nativeZh: 問自己是不是有點過頭了
examples: One more joke? Am I pushing it?
I asked for a discount, but I might be pushing it.
tags.usage: push it 表示把玩笑、要求或尺度再往前推一點。

segments.text: Ooh, it's like moving. This giant aircraft can literally just be pulled by a rope.
segments.en: Ooh, it's like moving. This giant aircraft can literally just be pulled by a rope.
segments.zh: 喔，它好像在動。這麼大的飛行器，居然可以用一條繩子拉著走。

tags.native: any flying machine, such as a plane or blimp
tags.nativeZh: 飛行器（飛機、飛船等的總稱）
examples: The aircraft is ready for boarding.
A blimp is a kind of aircraft.
tags.usage: 比 plane 更總稱、稍正式；單複數同形。

tags.v: can literally just be pulled by a rope
tags.native: emphasizing an surprisingly simple fact
tags.nativeZh: 強調「真的只用一條繩子就能拉」
examples: The cart can literally just be pulled by one person.
It's huge, but it can literally be moved by hand.
tags.usage: literally just 把難以置信的簡單動作講得很直白。

segments.text: Let's see if it stops floating when I get on it. That's gains, dude. Does that mean I'm fat?
segments.en: Let's see if it stops floating when I get on it. That's gains, dude. Does that mean I'm fat?
segments.zh: 看看我上去之後它還會不會浮著。那是增肌，兄弟。所以那是說我很胖嗎？

tags.native: gym slang meaning that's muscle you've built
tags.nativeZh: 健身圈口語：那是練出來的肌肉
examples: Those shoulders? That's gains, dude.
He looked at the photo and said, 'That's gains.'
tags.usage: gains 指增肌成果。這裡朋友拿來解釋飛船為什麼下沉，順便開玩笑。

segments.text: It means you work out a lot. — Or I'm fat. All right, let's do this. Goodbye, Chandler. Goodbye, forever. I think I heard forever.
segments.en: It means you work out a lot. — Or I'm fat. All right, let's do this. Goodbye, Chandler. Goodbye, forever. I think I heard forever.
segments.zh: 意思是你很常健身。——或者我很胖。好，我們開始吧。再見，Chandler。永遠再見。我好像聽到「永遠」。

tags.native: a dramatic, often joking farewell
examples: Goodbye, forever, my old phone.
He waved and said, 'Goodbye, forever.'
tags.usage: 語氣過火，所以聽的人會特別注意到 forever 這個詞。

segments.text: [Chris] He could have promoted anything and he chose Karl's mom. I'm terrified. This ain't picking up speed. Well, we'll see you at the race.
segments.en: [Chris] He could have promoted anything and he chose Karl's mom. I'm terrified. This ain't picking up speed. Well, we'll see you at the race.
segments.zh: [Chris] 他要宣傳什麼都行，結果選了 Karl 的媽媽。我嚇死了。這速度完全沒有起來。那我們比賽現場見。

tags.native: he had every option, but chose this one
tags.nativeZh: 他要宣傳什麼都行，結果選了這個
examples: She could have promoted anything, and she chose her dog.
He could have promoted the brand, but he didn't.
tags.usage: could have + 過去分詞，用來對比「明明有更好選擇」。

tags.native: this is not accelerating; informal ain't
examples: The bike ain't picking up speed.
We're moving, but we aren't picking up speed.
tags.usage: ain't = isn't / aren't / am not，很口語。pick up speed 就是加速。

segments.text: Oh, and I forgot to mention, we're flying this blimp over 150,000 people at the world's largest race car event.
segments.en: Oh, and I forgot to mention, we're flying this blimp over 150,000 people at the world's largest race car event.
segments.zh: 喔，我忘了說，我們要開著這艘飛船飛過十五萬人的頭頂，地點是全世界最大的賽車活動。

tags.native: used to add an important leftover detail
tags.nativeZh: 補上一句剛才忘了說的重點
examples: Oh, I forgot to mention: dinner is at seven.
I forgot to mention we're leaving early.
tags.usage: 常在 already 出發或故事中途，再補一個關鍵資訊。

segments.text: And Karl has no idea.
segments.en: And Karl has no idea.
segments.zh: 而且 Karl 完全不知道。

tags.native: is completely unaware
examples: He has no idea we're planning a party.
I had no idea the shop was closed.
tags.usage: have no idea 比 doesn't know 更強調「一點都不知道」。

segments.text: We are now over the Daytona 500 which is one of the busiest events ever. [Karl] You couldn't have put something better on the blimp. — No, this is perfect.
segments.en: We are now over the Daytona 500 which is one of the busiest events ever. [Karl] You couldn't have put something better on the blimp. — No, this is perfect.
segments.zh: 我們現在正在 Daytona 500 上空，這是最熱鬧的活動之一。[Karl] 你就不能在飛船上放點更好的東西嗎？——不，這樣最完美。

tags.native: a famous U.S. stock-car race in Daytona Beach, Florida
tags.nativeZh: 美國最知名的大賽車之一（戴通納 500）
examples: They're flying over the Daytona 500.
The Daytona 500 is packed every year.
tags.usage: 專有名詞，聽力裡碰到直接當活動名稱記即可。

segments.text: This is wrong. [Chris] Can they see us? [MrBeast] You can see 'em.
segments.en: This is wrong. [Chris] Can they see us? [MrBeast] You can see 'em.
segments.zh: 這不對。[Chris] 他們看得到我們嗎？[MrBeast] 你看得到他們。

tags.native: informal 'you can see them'
examples: Look down. You can see 'em from here.
I can't see 'em yet.
tags.usage: 'em 是 them 的口語弱讀，前面常接 see / tell / get。

segments.text: Karl, I can confirm. Everyone loves your mom down here. I love Karl's mom. Everybody's like, "We love..."
segments.en: Karl, I can confirm. Everyone loves your mom down here. I love Karl's mom. Everybody's like, "We love..."
segments.zh: Karl，我可以確認。下面每個人都愛你媽。我愛 Karl 的媽媽。大家都在喊：「我們愛……」

tags.native: a playful or formal-sounding way to back up a claim
tags.nativeZh: 我可以確認／我證實一下
examples: I can confirm the rumor is true.
I can confirm everyone had a good time.
tags.usage: 本是較正式用法，用在玩笑裡會有一點假裝一本正經的效果。

segments.text: [Crowd] I love Karl's mom. Karl's mom, if you're watching, you're a lovely lady.
segments.en: [Crowd] I love Karl's mom. Karl's mom, if you're watching, you're a lovely lady.
segments.zh: [觀眾] 我愛 Karl 的媽媽。Karl 的媽媽，如果你正在看，你是一位很可愛的女士。

tags.native: addressing someone who might be in the audience
tags.nativeZh: 對可能正在看的人直接喊話
examples: Mom, if you're watching, hi.
If you're watching at home, try this with us.
tags.usage: 直播、影片裡常拿來跟特定觀眾互動。

tags.native: a warm, polite compliment for a woman
tags.nativeZh: 對女士溫暖有禮的讚美
examples: Thank you, you're a lovely lady.
She's a lovely lady, and everyone likes her.
tags.usage: 語氣偏禮貌、老派一點，適合當眾示好，不帶輕浮。

segments.text: [Crowd] We love Karl's mom. And now, the most expensive private plane ticket on the planet.
segments.en: [Crowd] We love Karl's mom. And now, the most expensive private plane ticket on the planet.
segments.zh: [觀眾] 我們愛 Karl 的媽媽。接下來，地球上最貴的私人機票。

segments.text: Hi, welcome aboard. I suggest you take your shoes off. That carpet's actually $2 million. She's like, "I suggest it, really hard."
segments.en: Hi, welcome aboard. I suggest you take your shoes off. That carpet's actually $2 million. She's like, "I suggest it, really hard."
segments.zh: 嗨，歡迎登機。我建議你把鞋子脫掉。那塊地毯其實值兩百萬美元。她的語氣像在說：「我是認真建議你脫的。」

tags.native: the standard greeting when someone gets on a plane or ship
examples: Hi, welcome aboard. Please find your seat.
The captain welcomed us aboard.
tags.usage: 航空、遊輪的固定用語；官方字幕曾寫成 welcome board，正確是 aboard。

tags.native: a polite instruction that is still basically a request
tags.nativeZh: 禮貌地建議，其實常是在請你照做
examples: I suggest you take your seats.
I suggest you check the weather first.
tags.usage: 比 Please 稍軟、又比 You should 客氣。後面可接原形動詞。

segments.text: [MrBeast] And by square feet, this is bigger than our houses. It's almost impossible to imagine how big this jet actually is.
segments.en: [MrBeast] And by square feet, this is bigger than our houses. It's almost impossible to imagine how big this jet actually is.
segments.zh: [MrBeast] 而且以平方英尺來算，這比我們的房子還大。這架噴射機到底有多大，幾乎無法想像。

tags.native: measured according to floor area
examples: By square feet, this office is bigger than my apartment.
They price the shop by square feet.
tags.usage: 美國常用 square feet 講房屋或機艙面積。

tags.native: it is extremely hard to picture or believe
examples: It's almost impossible to imagine a jet this big.
It's almost impossible to imagine finishing tonight.
tags.usage: 用來強調規模或難度超出直覺。

segments.text: Right here is a bedroom. Wow. — A bedroom. Another bedroom, another bedroom. Keep going.
segments.en: Right here is a bedroom. Wow. — A bedroom. Another bedroom, another bedroom. Keep going.
segments.zh: 這裡是一間臥室。哇。——一間臥室。又一間臥室，又一間臥室。繼續走。

tags.native: don't stop; continue in the same direction
examples: Keep going down the hall.
You're doing great. Keep going.
tags.usage: 可以指方向，也可以當加油；這裡是帶路時叫人繼續往前。

segments.text: This is for the crew, another bedroom. Hoo! — What'd you find? My dibs? The bedrooms on this plane are way more extravagant.
segments.en: This is for the crew, another bedroom. Hoo! — What'd you find? My dibs? The bedrooms on this plane are way more extravagant.
segments.zh: 這是機組人員的，又一間臥室。呼！——你找到什麼？我先佔了？這架飛機上的臥室豪華得多。

tags.native: very fancy, luxurious, or more than necessary
examples: The decoration is a bit extravagant.
They threw an extravagant party.
tags.usage: 比 luxurious 多一點「過頭、超奢華」的意思。

tags.native: checking whether you can claim something first
examples: My dibs on that room?
I found the seat. My dibs?
tags.usage: 把 dibs 變成一句確認，有點得意、有點開玩笑。

segments.text: Gold plated sinks, multiple showers. Wait, what's in there? — That's the toilet. This plane comes with its own theater room, a lounge that can seat up to 12 people.
segments.en: Gold plated sinks, multiple showers. Wait, what's in there? — That's the toilet. This plane comes with its own theater room, a lounge that can seat up to 12 people.
segments.zh: 鍍金洗手台，好幾個淋浴間。等一下，那裡面是什麼？——那是馬桶。這架飛機還有專屬劇院、可以坐到十二人的休息室。

tags.native: covered with a thin layer of gold
examples: The faucet is gold plated.
It looks expensive, but it's only gold plated.
tags.usage: 複合形容詞，常寫 gold-plated。指表面鍍金，不一定是實心金。

tags.native: a room set up for watching films
examples: The house has a theater room in the basement.
The jet comes with its own theater room.
tags.usage: 私人住宅或豪華交通工具裡的家庭劇院空間。

segments.text: [MrBeast] And then over here is the living room. This is like a bigger couch than what I have in my house.
segments.en: [MrBeast] And then over here is the living room. This is like a bigger couch than what I have in my house.
segments.zh: [MrBeast] 然後這邊是客廳。這沙發比我家的還大。

tags.native: the main sitting room in a home
examples: They're watching TV in the living room.
This jet even has a living room.
tags.usage: 用家裡的房間名稱來形容飛機，是在強調它有多大、多像房子。

segments.text: I just want you to know you've only seen a third of the plane so far. There's more. [Chris] What? Oh, got some good stuff. You can call flight attendants in your bedroom.
segments.en: I just want you to know you've only seen a third of the plane so far. There's more. [Chris] What? Oh, got some good stuff. You can call flight attendants in your bedroom.
segments.zh: 我只是想讓你知道，到目前為止你才看過這架飛機的三分之一。還有更多。[Chris] 什麼？喔，有好東西。你可以在臥室裡呼叫空服員。

tags.native: one of three equal parts
examples: We've only seen a third of the museum.
A third of the class was absent.
tags.usage: 分數寫法是 a third of + 名詞。two thirds 是三分之二。

tags.native: found or noticed something impressive or enjoyable
examples: Oh, we got some good stuff in this box.
This playlist has some good stuff.
tags.usage: stuff 很口語，泛指不錯的內容或物品。

segments.text: If we could do this every time we fly, I'd live in the air. Whoa, whoa, what is that? Sorry, I'm turning the lights on and off. How did I miss this room?
segments.en: If we could do this every time we fly, I'd live in the air. Whoa, whoa, what is that? Sorry, I'm turning the lights on and off. How did I miss this room?
segments.zh: 如果每次搭飛機都能這樣，我願意住在天上。哇，哇，那是什麼？抱歉，我在開關燈。我怎麼會漏掉這個房間？

tags.native: I'd happily spend my life traveling by plane
tags.nativeZh: 我願意一直住在天上／一直飛行
examples: If every flight felt like this, I'd live in the air.
He loves airports so much he'd live in the air.
tags.usage: 誇張的假設句，用來表達有多享受當下。

tags.native: surprise that you somehow overlooked something obvious
examples: How did I miss this room on the tour?
How did I miss this email?
tags.usage: 帶一點自責或難以置信，適合用在找東西、參觀場合。

segments.text: Like we walked around the whole plane. And in case you thought you saw everything, there's also massages on this plane. How is it, Karl?
segments.en: Like we walked around the whole plane. And in case you thought you saw everything, there's also massages on this plane. How is it, Karl?
segments.zh: 我們明明把整架飛機走了一圈。而且如果你以為都看完了，這架飛機還有按摩。感覺如何，Karl？

tags.native: used to correct a wrong assumption before it settles
examples: And in case you thought we were done, there's dessert.
In case you thought I forgot, here's the file.
tags.usage: 先假設對方的想法，再補上更驚人的事實。

segments.text: It's amazing. So, I really just shouldn't.
segments.en: It's amazing. So, I really just shouldn't.
segments.zh: 太舒服了。所以我真的不該這樣。

segments.text: Gentlemen, how were we able to afford this plane? I would say only our fans. And because of that, we invited a bunch of random subscribers on this half a million-dollar plane ride.
segments.en: Gentlemen, how were we able to afford this plane? I would say only our fans. And because of that, we invited a bunch of random subscribers on this half a million-dollar plane ride.
segments.zh: 各位，我們怎麼負擔得起這架飛機？我只能說，全靠我們的粉絲。也因為這樣，我們邀請了一群隨機訂閱者，來搭這趟價值五十萬美元的飛機。

tags.v: how were we able to afford…
tags.native: asking what made an expensive thing possible
examples: How were we able to afford this trip?
I still don't know how they were able to afford the upgrade.
tags.usage: be able to afford 是談金錢能力的穩妥說法。

tags.native: people who follow a channel or service
examples: They invited random subscribers on the trip.
The channel has a million subscribers.
tags.usage: YouTube 場景的核心詞；subscribe 是對應動詞。

segments.text: Have you ever flown on a private jet before? No. This is my first time. And it's the most expensive one on the planet.
segments.en: Have you ever flown on a private jet before? No. This is my first time. And it's the most expensive one on the planet.
segments.zh: 你以前坐過私人飛機嗎？沒有。這是我第一次。而且還是地球上最貴的那一架。

tags.native: asking if someone has had a particular travel experience
tags.nativeZh: 問對方有沒有搭過某種交通工具
examples: Have you ever flown on a private jet before?
Have you ever flown on a red-eye?
tags.usage: Have you ever + 過去分詞，是分享經歷前最自然的開場。

segments.text: I've never seen anything like this on a plane. Like this is crazy. [Karl] What the heck is over this way? [Chris] Yo, this gotta be a secret room.
segments.en: I've never seen anything like this on a plane. Like this is crazy. [Karl] What the heck is over this way? [Chris] Yo, this gotta be a secret room.
segments.zh: 我在飛機上從沒見過這種東西。這太狂了。[Karl] 這邊到底是什麼？[Chris] 唷，這肯定是密道房間。

tags.native: a milder way to say 'what the hell' when confused or surprised
tags.nativeZh: 驚訝或困惑時較溫和的咒罵替代
examples: What the heck is that noise?
What the heck happened here?
tags.usage: 比 what the hell 客氣，仍偏口語，不適合很正式的場合。

tags.native: informal 'this has got to be' / 'this must be'
examples: This gotta be the exit.
This has got to be a joke.
tags.usage: 完整一點是 this has got to be 或 this has gotta be；省略 has 很口語。

segments.text: That's where the crew is. We just got a bunch of funny looks. Attention, boys. We're about to take off.
segments.en: That's where the crew is. We just got a bunch of funny looks. Attention, boys. We're about to take off.
segments.zh: 那是機組人員的地方。我們剛剛換來一堆奇怪的眼神。注意了，男孩子們。我們即將起飛。

tags.native: strange or disapproving glances from other people
tags.nativeZh: 別人投來的古怪／不以為然的眼神
examples: We got a few funny looks in the elevator.
Wear that hat and you'll get funny looks.
tags.usage: funny 這裡不是「好笑」，而是「怪異、耐人尋味」。

tags.native: we will leave the ground very soon
examples: Please sit down. We're about to take off.
We're about to take off, so text you later.
tags.usage: be about to 表示馬上要發生，航空廣播超常用。

segments.text: Fasten your seat belts, stop being hooligans. Thank you.
segments.en: Fasten your seat belts, stop being hooligans. Thank you.
segments.zh: 請繫好安全帶，別再當小混混了。謝謝。

tags.native: the standard instruction to buckle up
examples: Fasten your seat belts and return your trays.
The sign tells you to fasten your seat belt.
tags.usage: 比 keep your seatbelt on 更像正式廣播用語。

tags.native: people behaving in a rowdy, mischievous, or disorderly way
tags.nativeZh: 搗蛋鬼、鬧事的人（常是半開玩笑）
examples: Stop being hooligans and sit down.
A few hooligans were shouting in the street.
tags.usage: 本義偏負面，朋友間或機長喊話時也可以帶點戲謔。

segments.text: At this price point, they serve the highest quality food anytime you want it and wherever on the plane you want it.
segments.en: At this price point, they serve the highest quality food anytime you want it and wherever on the plane you want it.
segments.zh: 到了這個價位，他們會在你想吃的任何時間、飛機上的任何位置，提供最高品質的餐點。

tags.native: available at whatever time you choose
tags.nativeZh: 你想什麼時候要都可以
examples: You can order room service anytime you want it.
The car is ready anytime you want it.
tags.usage: 和 wherever 搭配時，強調時間和地點都完全自由。

segments.text: Even in your own private master suite. You want some?
segments.en: Even in your own private master suite. You want some?
segments.zh: 就算在你自己的私人主套房裡也可以。要來一點嗎？

tags.native: the largest, most private bedroom, often with its own bathroom
examples: The master suite has a huge window.
Guests stayed in the master suite.
tags.usage: 房屋和豪華交通工具都用，比 bedroom 更高一級。

segments.text: Do you guys even know where we're going? [Group] No. We're taking you all to Disney World and we're gonna give you two days of all expense paid trips to do whatever you want.
segments.en: Do you guys even know where we're going? [Group] No. We're taking you all to Disney World and we're gonna give you two days of all expense paid trips to do whatever you want.
segments.zh: 你們知道我們要去哪嗎？[眾人] 不知道。我們要帶你們去迪士尼世界，再給你們兩天一切費用全包的行程，想做什麼都可以。

tags.native: someone else pays every cost of the trip
examples: She won an all-expense-paid vacation.
They're giving us two days, all expenses paid.
tags.usage: 常見寫法是 all-expenses-paid；口語也會說 all expense paid。

segments.text: No way. So, if you wanna fly on the most expensive jet in the world and then spend two days all paid for in Disney World, subscribe.
segments.en: No way. So, if you wanna fly on the most expensive jet in the world and then spend two days all paid for in Disney World, subscribe.
segments.zh: 不可能吧。所以，如果你想坐世界上最貴的噴射機，再花兩天在迪士尼世界盡情玩、全部免費，記得訂閱。

tags.native: a call to action that ties the wish to hitting subscribe
tags.nativeZh: 把願望和「請訂閱」綁在一起的行動呼籲
examples: If you wanna see the next trip, subscribe.
If you wanna come with us next time, subscribe.
tags.usage: YouTube 片尾超典型：wanna = want to，最後收在 subscribe。
